(I) Initial discovery and early extraction: rapid exponential growth as easily accessible, shallow reserves are tapped
(II) Peak Production (Hubbert Peak): maximum extraction rate is reached when approximately half of all recoverable reserves are exhausted
(III) Post-Peak Deceleration: production begins irreversible terminal decline as remaining reserves become deeper and costlier to extract
(IV) Economic depletion / Abandonment: energy return on investment (EROI) collapses near 1:1, rendering remaining reserves economically unviable

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: I -> III -> II -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: II -> I -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: IV -> II -> III -> I
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: I -> II -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Hubbert curve progression: discovery boom, peak production, post-peak contraction, and economic exhaustion when EROI collapses.
Hence Option C is correct.
Hence, option (D) is correct.

questionText:
Match the fossil fuel in List I with its primary hydrocarbon chemical component in List II:

List I:
(A) Natural Gas
(B) Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG)
(C) Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)
(D) Biogas

List II:
(I) Methane (CH4, approx. 70–90%)
(II) Propane (C3H8) and Butane (C4H10) compressed under moderate pressure
(III) Methane (CH4) compressed to 200–250 bar pressure for vehicular transport
(IV) Methane (55–70%) mixed with Carbon Dioxide (30–45%) from anaerobic digestion

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Natural gas and CNG are predominantly methane (CH4); LPG is propane/butane; and biogas is biologically generated methane and CO2.
Hence Option B is correct.
Hence, option (C) is the correct match.

topic: Process Flow of a Carbon Offset Project under Verra (VCS) or Gold Standard
questionText:

questionText:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) programs create market incentives for environmental conservation.
Reason (R): Upstream forest stewards and watershed landowners are financially compensated by downstream water users (cities, hydroelectric plants) for maintaining forest cover that filters water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Validates both statements and confirms causal explanation.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to notice that Reason does not causally explain the Assertion.

options.text: (A) is true but (R) is false
options.mistakeAnalysis: Accepted an inaccurate Reason as factually true.

options.text: (A) is false but (R) is true
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to identify the scientific fallacy in the Assertion.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) correctly explains (A). PES (e.g. Costa Rica's Pagos por Servicios Ambientales) compensates resource managers for positive conservation externalities.
Hence Option C is correct.
Hence, option (A) is the correct choice.
